title: Raspberry and Cream Cheese Danish Pastries
summary: Flaky, laminated Danish pastries twisted into golden coils and filled with a tangy baked cream cheese filling studded with fresh raspberries.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook (or large bowl)
2 baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
large egg, beaten with 1 tbsp milk

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, salt and cardamom in a stand mixer bowl, then add the alcohol-free vanilla extract, egg, cold milk, water and softened butter. Knead with the dough hook for 4-5 minutes until the dough is smooth and soft. Keeping the milk and water cold stops the dough warming up, which matters once the butter needs to stay firm for lamination.

steps.title: First chill
steps.text: Pat the dough into a rectangle about 2cm thick, wrap in cling film and chill for 2 hours, or overnight. This firms the dough right through, so it won't soften and melt the butter block during the first roll.

steps.title: Prepare the butter block
steps.text: Beat the cold butter between two sheets of baking paper with the rolling pin, then shape it into a neat 15 x 15cm square. Chill for 20 minutes until it feels firm but still bends without cracking - the texture needed for clean lamination.

steps.title: Encase the butter
steps.text: Roll the chilled dough into a 30 x 15cm rectangle, lay the butter square over one half, fold the other half over and pinch the edges to seal. Sealing it in now keeps the butter as a distinct layer, rather than squeezing out as you roll.

steps.title: First and second turns
steps.text: Roll the dough out to 45 x 20cm and fold it in thirds like a letter, then wrap and chill for 30 minutes. Repeat the roll-and-fold twice more, for three single turns in total, chilling between each one and for longer if the butter starts to soften or smear. These folds build the alternating dough and butter layers that will puff apart in the oven.

steps.title: Final rest
steps.text: Chill the laminated dough for 1 hour after the last fold so it firms up completely before shaping. A properly rested dough rolls out cleanly, without the layers dragging or tearing.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Beat the cream cheese, sugar, egg yolk, lemon zest and alcohol-free vanilla extract together until smooth and thick. This tangy filling sets as it bakes, giving a rich, slightly firm centre rather than a runny one.

steps.title: Shape the coils
steps.text: Roll the dough into a 36 x 30cm rectangle about 5mm thick and cut it into 12 strips, each 2.5 x 30cm. Twist each strip several times, coil it loosely into a 9cm round, tuck the end underneath, then space the coils out well on the lined trays.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Cover the coils loosely and leave them somewhere warm, around 24-26°C, for 1-1½ hours, until they look puffy and feel wobbly when the tray is nudged. Keeping the room no hotter than this protects the butter layers - anything warmer and the butter melts into the dough instead of staying separate.

steps.title: Fill the wells
steps.text: Press a deep 5cm well into the centre of each coil with the back of a floured spoon, brush the twisted rims with egg wash, then spoon about 1½ tablespoons of filling into each well. The egg wash on the rims is what turns glossy and deep golden as it bakes.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and bake for 10 minutes, then press 3 raspberries into the filling of each pastry and bake for a further 6-10 minutes. They're ready when the pastry is deep golden and crisp at the edges, the filling is set and just firm at the edge, and a thermometer reads at least 71°C in the centre of the filling and about 90°C in the pastry itself.

steps.title: Cool and set
steps.text: Leave the pastries on the trays for 10 minutes, then move them to a wire rack for at least 20 minutes so the filling finishes setting. Cutting in too soon leaves the centre soft and slumped rather than sliced cleanly.

tips: Keep the butter block cold and firm through every turn - if it softens and smears into the dough, chill the whole lot for longer before rolling again, or you'll lose the distinct flaky layers.
Press the centre well deep enough (about 5cm) so the filling has somewhere to sit; a shallow well is a common mistake that lets the cheese filling spill over the sides as it bakes.
Prove in a spot no warmer than 24-26°C - any hotter and the butter layers melt into the dough before baking.
Check both temperatures at the end of baking: the filling should read at least 71°C and the pastry itself around 90°C.
These are best eaten the day they're baked, while the pastry is at its flakiest.
storage: Keep in the fridge because of the cream cheese filling, and eat on the day of baking for the best texture. Store leftovers airtight in the fridge for up to 1 day and refresh for 5 minutes in a 180°C oven until piping hot, or freeze baked pastries for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
